review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner (self-review after independent findings)
review.decision: Cover the actual bridge warning route, the protected compose behavior, and recovery after a retention append
review.notes: Independent review reproduced stderr contamination by removing the Run wiring and reproduced lost re-arming after the debug ceiling marker. Exercise the public Run function with private socket addresses and a normally exiting fake frontend. Signals and new storage-probe behavior are outside this change. Use disposable HOME and tmux state, synthetic disk-full errors and a sparse segment with a bounded tail read.

cases.description: The real Codex bridge entry keeps diagnostic failures away from inherited stderr
cases.setup: Launch the test in a subprocess with a disposable HOME, short private listener directory, a fake frontend and an unusable diagnostic segment. Run with a listening system-log socket and a missing socket.
cases.action: Call the public Run entry point, collect shared stderr and the child exit status, and read the launch counter and any system warning.
cases.expected: Each child starts once and returns its original normal exit code. Its own stderr is preserved. With a listener, a diagnostic warning reaches the socket. Neither case adds a gtmux warning to shared stderr. Removing the route installation from Run fails this test.

cases.description: An actual retention marker append re-arms a disk-full warning
cases.setup: Use a disposable store, a sparse segment at the debug ceiling and a synthetic ENOSPC warning.
cases.action: Report a full volume, try an unsuccessful internal append, then trigger the debug ceiling marker and verify its bounded on-disk tail before reporting ENOSPC again.
cases.expected: An unsuccessful append does not re-arm the existing warning. The marker is actually appended without the dropped debug entry. The next disk-full incident emits a second warning. The old retention write path fails this test.

cases.description: Protected send distinguishes an empty composer from manually typed bytes
cases.setup: Use a private tmux server and a fake foreground composer that records the line actually submitted.
cases.action: Use the protected send flow on an empty pane and on a pane seeded with a manually typed draft.
cases.expected: The empty composer receives the exact payload and one Enter. The draft is refused before any paste, Enter or clear. Its input bytes remain unchanged.
